item.title: Beijing turns recyclables into public seats, eyeing circular economy
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-25
BEIJING, Nov. 25 (Xinhua) -- Since the start of the year, Beijing has installed 48 eco-friendly benches made from recycled materials across 26 public spaces, as part of the capital's efforts to promote waste sorting and build a circular economy. The public spaces span historic streets, city parks, waterfront greenways and commercial plazas in seven districts, namely Dongcheng, Xicheng, Chaoyang, Haidian, Fengtai, Shijingshan and Tongzhou, the Beijing Municipal Commission of Urban Management said. The recycled seats come in two main types. The "cloud benches" are made from polypropylene materials such as recycled takeout boxes and plastic drink cups, which go through washing, shredding, modification and injection molding. Each contains material recycled from roughly 1,000 takeout containers. The "board benches" are made from milk cartons that are sorted, stripped of their aluminum and plastic layers, and crushed before being hot-pressed into recycled composite board. Each recycled seat features a sign explaining where its recycled materials came from and how much was used. Beijing has been expanding its recyclables collection system in recent years, linking neighborhood drop-off points, transfer stations and sorting centers so that low-value recyclables such as plastic takeout boxes and drink cups can be collected, transported and processed. This takeout-container recycling network now covers more than 20 universities, parks and railway stations, over 140 office buildings and 11,207 communities with recycling machines. The capital has also launched a citywide online recycling platform that lets residents book door-to-door pickup for old furniture, renovation waste and used appliances, and publishes prices for recyclables such as paper, plastic, metal and textiles. "What matters in building a full recycling chain is not making end products into showpieces, but giving residents feedback when they sort and letting them see the results in public spaces, so that sorting continues to be turned into resources," said Liu Jie, an official with the Beijing Municipal Commission of Urban Management. According to the commission, Beijing will add more recycled benches in more places, including upgraded neighborhoods, improved parks and commercial areas with better walking and cycling routes, while continuing to strengthen its recyclables collection system. ■

item.title: China's manufacturing powerhouse deepens regional integration
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-25
SHENZHEN, Nov. 25 (Xinhua) -- At 8 a.m., Yuan Moli leaves Shenzhen for work. Forty minutes later, she is in Zhongshan, another city across the Pearl River Estuary in south China's Guangdong Province. What was once a journey of more than two hours on the road has been dramatically shortened after the opening of the 24-kilometer Shenzhen-Zhongshan Link in June 2024. Yuan works for Xinyichang, a leading Chinese maker of LED die-bonding equipment. The company has built a production base in Zhongshan, which began operations in 2022. About 90 percent of the company's production lines have been moved to Zhongshan, Yuan said. Engineers can test equipment there in the morning and return to Shenzhen for research work in the afternoon, allowing research and manufacturing teams to work more closely together. The company's cross-city operations reflect a broader shift in the Pearl River Delta, one of the world's major manufacturing hubs, where improved transport links are helping cities in the region make better use of their respective strengths. BRIDGING THE DIVIDE The Pearl River Estuary, shaped like an inverted V, divides the Pearl River Delta into eastern and western banks. Shenzhen and Dongguan lie to the east, while Zhuhai, Zhongshan and Jiangmen are in the west. Though only dozens of kilometers apart in a straight line, these cities were long separated by lengthy road detours, with some journeys exceeding 200 kilometers. Benefiting from deepwater ports and proximity to Hong Kong, the eastern bank developed strengths in advanced manufacturing and technological innovation but faces limited room for expansion and rising costs. The western bank, meanwhile, has more land for industrial development but faces pressure to upgrade its industries and find new sources of growth. Before the Humen Bridge opened in 1997, the divide had been particularly evident in transportation. Drivers sometimes had to wait six or seven hours just to board a ferry. The bridge shortened road journeys between the two shores by roughly 120 kilometers, but growing traffic soon strained its capacity. More crossings followed, including the Nansha Bridge and the Hong Kong-Zhuhai-Macao Bridge. The opening of the Shenzhen-Zhongshan Link marked another major step. Completed after seven years of construction, this crossing combines bridges, artificial islands, an undersea tunnel and an underwater interchange. It cuts the drive between Shenzhen and Zhongshan from over two hours to around 30 minutes, making it much easier for people and businesses to move between the two cities. Since its opening in 2024, the transport artery has handled more than 81 million vehicle trips, according to local authorities. Zhu Wei, deputy director of Guangdong's provincial development and reform commission, compared the over 10 existing and planned crossings to shoelaces gradually pulling the eastern and western shores of the estuary closer together. INTEGRATED DEVELOPMENT Better transport connections are facilitating companies expanding across the estuary, tapping both Shenzhen's technological strengths and Zhongshan's manufacturing capacity and industrial space. Liao Lei, chairman of Shenzhen Seals Instrumentation Co., Ltd., a maker of precision testing equipment, recalled the difficulties of expanding in Shenzhen. "In Shenzhen, factory space was so limited that we couldn't set up multiple product testing lines," he said. After expanding to Zhongshan, the company increased its factory space from 700 square meters to more than 20,000 square meters, quadrupled its monthly production capacity from 500 to 2,000 units, and expanded its workforce from about 180 to over 460. "With enough room to build testing platforms, we can pursue more detailed research and develop several new product lines at the same time," Liao said. New industrial parks are also helping deepen cross-city industrial ties. On Ma'an Island in Zhongshan, near the Shenzhen-Zhongshan Link, the future technology center of the bay area is bringing businesses from the two cities together. The park opened in December 2024 with an investment of roughly 2.7 billion yuan (around 402 million U.S. dollars) to focus on smart manufacturing, medical devices, electronics, electrical equipment and information technology. It has attracted 30 companies, including one publicly listed company and two national-level "little giant" enterprises. Such cooperation is taking place in a region with a strong track record in innovation. The Shenzhen-Hong Kong-Guangzhou innovation cluster has once again ranked first among the world's top 100 innovation clusters in 2026, while the Macao-Zhuhai cluster made the top 100 for the third consecutive year, according to the World Intellectual Property Organization's Global Innovation Index. The Guangdong-Hong Kong-Macao Greater Bay Area comprises the Hong Kong and Macao special administrative regions and nine cities in Guangdong's Pearl River Delta. The region generates approximately one-ninth of China's GDP with less than 1 percent of the country's land area and 6 percent of its population. In September 2025, China's State Council approved comprehensive pilot reforms for market-based allocation of production factors in 10 regions, including the nine mainland cities of the Greater Bay Area. The pilot program seeks to remove institutional barriers to the free flow and efficient allocation of production factors, covering technology, land, labor, data, capital, and resources and environment. For companies like Xinyichang, closer integration is already changing how they operate. With Shenzhen's innovation resources and Zhongshan's manufacturing capacity now more closely connected, companies will have more room to grow and put down deeper roots, Yuan said. ■

item.title: Flying high and far to bright future for APEC
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-25
The world's attention turns to China as the 33rd APEC Economic Leaders' Meeting in Shenzhen, the City of the Roc (named after a legendary bird of great size and strength), delivers fruitful outcomes and marks a new peak in Asia-Pacific economic cooperation. Openness, innovation and cooperation are the priorities of China's APEC 2026 . With joint efforts to meet challenges facing development through opening up, generate momentum for growth through innovation, and pursue prosperity for all through cooperation, we look forward to seeing Asia-Pacific cooperation spread its wings like the roc and fly high and far to a bright future.

item.title: Exhibition highlights contributions of international friends in wartime China
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-25
A special exhibition revisits a pivotal chapter in China's revolutionary history -- through the eyes of Western journalists who witnessed it. "The Great Bridge-Builder -- Edgar Snow and International Friends in Yan'an" opened in Beijing, as this year marks the 90th anniversary of the Long March victory and of Snow's first trip to northern Shaanxi. ■

item.title: China to harness new technologies in national defense education
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-25
BEIJING, Nov. 25 (Xinhua) -- China will make greater use of emerging technologies and digital applications to promote public awareness of national defense over the next five years, according to a new plan aimed at strengthening relevant education and improving citizens' defense-related knowledge and skills. The plan, covering the 15th Five-Year Plan period (2026-2030), was jointly issued by the Publicity Department of the Communist Party of China Central Committee and the defense mobilization department of the Central Military Commission. It sets targets for the national defense education system and mechanisms to be further enhanced by 2030, with improved programs in relevant fields both at schools and among the public. It also calls for stronger coordination between military and civilian sectors in relevant efforts. The plan outlines seven key areas of work, including promoting relevant awareness among different groups of people, broadening practical educational activities, and making better use of the military's resources for educational purposes. It also stresses the importance of upholding the Party's overall leadership and implementing a holistic approach to national security. China's 15th Five-Year Plan calls for further raising public awareness of national defense and strengthening the unity between the military and the government, and between the military and the people. The country in 2001 adopted its National Defense Education Law, which underwent an amendment in 2018 and a revision in 2024. In 2023, several authorities started to jointly designate September as national defense education month. During the 2026 campaign, relevant authorities, institutions and schools across China organized a range of activities for public awareness promotion, such as airing educational videos and shows, and arranging student visits to revolutionary bases and memorial sites. Some military units also held open days, allowing members of the public to visit military barracks, naval ports and warships. ■

item.title: Tariff and trade wars serve no one's interests: Chinese FM spokesperson
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-25
BEIJING, Nov. 25 (Xinhua) -- Tariff wars and trade wars serve no one's interests, Chinese Foreign Ministry spokesperson Guo Jiakun said on Wednesday. Guo made the remarks at a regular news briefing when asked to comment on reports that the U.S. is set to announce tariffs on goods from China and some other countries. Guo stated that when it comes to handling the economic and trade issues between China and the United States, China's position is consistent and clear. Both sides should resolve relevant issues through consultation on the basis of equality, respect and mutual benefit. The so-called issue of overcapacity is a false proposition, and China opposes using it as a pretext for political manipulation. The two sides should work together to deliver on the important common understandings between the two heads of state and maintain the steady growth momentum of China-U.S. economic and trade relations, he added. ■

item.title: Shenzhou-24 astronauts, including first foreigner, enter China's Tiangong space station
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-25
FOCUS | Shenzhou-24 astronauts, including first foreigner, enter China's Tiangong space station-Xinhua FOCUS | Shenzhou-24 astronauts, including first foreigner, enter China's Tiangong space station Source: Xinhua Editor: huaxia 2026-11-25 18:01:30 JIUQUAN, Nov. 25 (Xinhua) -- The Shenzhou-24 crew, comprising Chinese astronauts Tang Hongbo and Wu Yi, and Pakistani astronaut Muhammad Zeeshan Ali, entered China's Tiangong space station on Wednesday. Serving as a payload specialist, Ali has made history by becoming the first foreigner to board Tiangong. The astronaut trio took off at 8:18 a.m. (Beijing Time) the same day aboard China's Shenzhou-24 spaceship from the Jiuquan Satellite Launch Center in northwest China. The Shenzhou-23 crew in orbit opened the hatch of the space station at 2:35 p.m. and welcomed the new arrivals, according to the China Manned Space Agency (CMSA). After entering the space station, the Shenzhou-24 crew met with the three Shenzhou-23 astronauts, who have been in orbit for about six months. The two crews then took group pictures of the ninth space get-together in China's aerospace history. They will now start a new in-orbit handover round.

item.title: Xi says joint space exploration by Chinese, Pakistani astronauts vivid embodiment of deep-rooted friendship
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-25
BEIJING, Nov. 25 (Xinhua) -- Chinese President Xi Jinping said on Wednesday that the joint space exploration by astronauts from China and Pakistan is a vivid embodiment of the deep-rooted friendship between the two countries. It marks another important achievement in bilateral cooperation, Xi said while exchanging congratulations with Pakistani President Asif Ali Zardari on the joint spaceflight mission. In the message, Xi said that he was glad to learn of a Pakistani astronaut's successful entry into space aboard a Chinese Shenzhou spaceship for the first time, making him the first foreign astronaut to inhabit China's space station. Xi extended his warm congratulations to the Pakistani government and people, as well as to astronauts and space professionals from both countries on behalf of the Chinese government and people. Xi noted that China and Pakistan are all-weather strategic cooperative partners, saying that the friendship between the two countries has remained rock-solid and unbreakable since diplomatic ties were established 75 years ago. Emphasizing that China's space station is an ark of peace, friendship and cooperation, Xi said that China stands ready to work with Pakistan and other countries to advance the peaceful use of outer space, deepen international space cooperation, and improve global governance in outer space, to ensure that outer space exploration delivers greater benefits to the humanity. For his part, Zardari expressed profound appreciation to the Chinese government and the brotherly Chinese people on behalf of the Pakistani government and people. He said the historic space cooperation between Pakistan and China and the first Pakistani astronaut entering China's space station come as the two countries commemorate the 75th anniversary of the establishment of diplomatic relations. Such cooperation demonstrates China's remarkable progress in space science and technology, its firm commitment to the peaceful use of outer space, and the significance of building a community with a shared future for humanity, Zardari said, adding that it will further strengthen bilateral friendship, and promote the all-weather strategic cooperative partnership between the two countries to a higher level. ■

item.title: Xi urges advancing building of Party regulations, institutions
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-25
BEIJING, Nov. 25 (Xinhua) -- Chinese President Xi Jinping has urged continuous and high-quality advancement in the building of regulations and institutions of the Communist Party of China (CPC), and upholding rule-based governance as the basic approach to governing the Party. Xi, also general secretary of the CPC Central Committee and chairman of the Central Military Commission, made the remarks in a recent instruction on the work related to Party regulations and institutions. Xi said the CPC has made solid efforts and achieved notable achievements in strengthening Party regulations and institutions over the past five years. To provide institutional guarantees for persevering with full and rigorous Party self-governance and ensuring the Party remains the strong leadership core in building socialism with Chinese characteristics, Xi urged enhanced efforts in the systematic integration, education and enforcement of Party institutions, as well as in improving the alignment and coordination of Party rules and regulations with state laws and regulations. Xi's instruction was conveyed at a national meeting on the work related to Party regulations held in Beijing on Tuesday and Wednesday. Cai Qi, a member of the Standing Committee of the Political Bureau of the Communist Party of China (CPC) Central Committee and a member of the Secretariat of the CPC Central Committee, attends and addresses a national meeting on the work related to Party regulations in Beijing, capital of China. An important instruction by Chinese President Xi Jinping, also general secretary of the CPC Central Committee and chairman of the Central Military Commission, was conveyed at the meeting held in Beijing on Tuesday and Wednesday. (Xinhua/Yue Yuewei) Cai Qi, a member of the Standing Committee of the Political Bureau of the CPC Central Committee and a member of the Secretariat of the CPC Central Committee, attended and addressed the meeting. Running the Party through institutions and regulations is one of the core meanings of Xi Jinping Thought on Party Building, Cai noted, calling for efforts to enhance the level of running the Party through regulations across the board. ■
